paraphrase: Make me your treasurer, Mother; I am not the kind to betray my salt — the devotee asks to be the keeper of the Mother's treasure, her feet.
speaker: Rāmprasād
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording varies between collections

location.section: song 'Ḍub de re man Kālī bale'

paraphrase: Dive deep, O mind, saying 'Kālī', into the fathomless waters of the heart's ocean of jewels; if you find no jewels at first, do not think the ocean empty.
notes: Commonly attributed to Rāmprasād; attribution uncertain.
speaker: Rāmprasād
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording varies between collections

paraphrase: This world is a frame of illusion (dhokār ṭāṭi): the singer warns the mind not to be deceived by what passes, and turns to the Mother.
notes: The Vaiṣṇava Āju Gosāi is said to have answered with 'Ei saṃsār majār kuṭi' ('this world is a mansion of mirth'); Ramakrishna later cited both (U52).
speaker: Rāmprasād
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording varies between collections

paraphrase: How long, Mother, will you make me go round like the blindfolded ox of the oil-press? Bound to the post of the world I turn and turn — the singer pleads to be released from the round of births.
speaker: Rāmprasād
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording varies between collections

location.section: song 'Mana re kṛṣi kāj jāno nā'

paraphrase: O mind, you do not know how to farm: this field of human life lies fallow; had you cultivated it, gold would have grown. Fence it with Kālī's name so the crop is not stolen.
speaker: Rāmprasād
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording varies between collections
